```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

brandkit gives a Shiny app its theme through three page functions that
replace the bslib ones. This article covers them, the optional "drift" look,
how light and dark mode reach your plots and widgets, and the four app
templates.

## Page wrappers

| brandkit | Replaces | `...` takes |
|---|---|---|
| `brand_page_sidebar()` | `bslib::page_sidebar()` | any UI (plus `sidebar =`) |
| `brand_page_navbar()` | `bslib::page_navbar()` | `nav_panel()` / `nav_menu()` items only |
| `brand_page_fluid()` | `bslib::page_fluid()` | any UI |

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(ggplot2)
library(brandkit)

ui <- brand_page_sidebar(
  title = "New York air quality",
  sidebar = sidebar(selectInput("var", "Variable", c("Temp", "Wind", "Solar.R"))),
  card(card_header("Ozone"), plotOutput("plot"))
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    ggplot(airquality, aes(.data[[input$var]], Ozone)) + geom_point(size = 3)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

There is no `theme =`, no `+ theme_brand()`, no colour scale and no dark-mode
code. Each wrapper does this for you:

1. Builds the bslib Bootstrap 5 theme from `_brand.yml` (`brand_theme()`).
2. Injects dark-mode CSS for the datepicker (`brand_dark_css()`).
3. Adds a dark-mode toggle, fixed to the top right.
4. Puts the brand logo next to the title, if there is one.
5. Switches on `thematic`, so every `renderPlot()` gets the brand font and a
   background matching its card. Discrete colour and fill scales pick the
   brand's light or dark palette according to the card the plot sits on.
6. Hides plots while they lay out for the first time, so they don't flash at
   the wrong size.
7. Sets the app-wide ggplot theme to the opaque `theme_brand(transparent =
   FALSE)`, which thematic needs to repaint plot backgrounds.

All three take `title`, `logo`, `dark_mode`, `dark_mode_id`, `theme_args`
(extra arguments for `brand_theme()`) and `style`. `brand_page_sidebar()` also
takes `fillable`.

A navbar page only accepts navigation items. Content that isn't inside a
`nav_panel()` fails with *"Navigation containers expect a collection of
nav_panel()s"*:

```{r}
# Fails
brand_page_navbar(title = "App", card("content"), nav_panel("Tab", "..."))

# Works
brand_page_navbar(title = "App", nav_panel("Main", card("content")))
```

### The "drift" style

`style = "drift"` is the poster template's look in the browser. It is opt-in;
`"classic"` (the default) leaves the page as bslib draws it.

```{r}
brand_page_sidebar(title = "App", sidebar = sidebar(), style = "drift")
```

What it changes:

- Soft **corner ornaments** at the top right and bottom left of the window,
  drawn in the brand colours and following the dark-mode toggle (also
  available alone as `brand_ornaments_tag()`).
- A **plain-type title**: the navbar's bar and rule go, so the title sits on
  the page with the ornament behind it.
- **Cards as tinted surfaces**: the brand's primary mixed 7% into the
  background, a solid header, no shadow.
- A **transparent sidebar**, so the bottom-left ornament shows through.
- **Tables and text output** take the card colour, with a faint stripe.

Everything is scoped to a class the page adds to `<html>`, so it can't leak
into a classic page. On a fluid page there is no bar, so you get the ornaments,
cards and tables.

## Light and dark mode

### Plots drawn with `renderPlot()`

Nothing to do. `thematic` reads the colours of the card each plot sits on and
redraws it when the mode changes, theme, discrete palette and background
included.

### Anything that needs to know the mode

`brand_dark_mode()` gives you the current mode as a reactive, for outputs
Bootstrap and thematic can't reach: plotly, gt tables, leaflet palettes, base
graphics and file downloads.

```{r}
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  dm <- brand_dark_mode(input)       # dm$mode() is "light" or "dark"

  output$p <- plotly::renderPlotly({
    mode <- dm$mode()
    p <- ggplot(airquality, aes(Temp, Ozone, colour = factor(Month))) +
      geom_point() +
      scale_color_brand_d(mode = mode)
    brand_plotly(p, mode = mode, tooltip = c("x", "y"))
  })
}
```

| Output | What to do |
|---|---|
| `renderPlot()` with ggplot2 | nothing |
| HTML and Bootstrap UI | nothing (CSS variables follow the mode) |
| DT tables | nothing (with `class = "table-striped"`) |
| `brand_plotly()` | pass `mode = dm$mode()` |
| gt tables | style with `brand_colors(mode)` |
| leaflet | pass `mode` to `brand_pal_seq()`, and choose tiles by mode |
| base `plot()` / `barplot()` | use `brand_colors(mode)` for `col.axis` and so on |
| downloads | `ggsave(bg = brand_colors(mode)$background)` |

## Interactive plots

`brand_plotly()` converts a ggplot to a plotly widget with brand colours,
fonts and grid. In a Shiny *app*, pass `mode` as above. In a Quarto dashboard
(`server: shiny`) leave `mode` out: it reads the background of the card it sits
on (see `vignette("quarto-documents")`). Plotly's tooltip for a continuous colour
scale needs `tooltip = c("x", "y")`; adding `"colour"` only works for discrete
colours.

## Tables

DT inherits Bootstrap's styling, and brandkit's CSS covers its pagination,
search box and stripes in both modes:

```{r}
DT::datatable(airquality, class = "table-striped", rownames = FALSE,
              options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "tip"))
```

gt ignores Bootstrap's variables, so style it from the brand:

```{r}
cols <- brand_colors(mode)

gt::gt(head(airquality)) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = list(gt::cell_fill(color = cols$primary),
                 gt::cell_text(color = "white", weight = "bold")),
    locations = gt::cells_column_labels()
  ) |>
  gt::tab_options(
    table.background.color = cols$background,
    table.width = gt::pct(100)
  )
```

## Maps

leaflet maps sit outside Bootstrap, but brandkit supplies a marker palette
(`brand_pal_seq()`, which takes `mode`) and dark-mode CSS for the zoom buttons,
attribution and legend. Pick the tiles by mode too. CARTO's `Positron` and
`DarkMatter` basemaps now need an API key and watermark every tile without
one, so use Esri's keyless grey canvas, which has a light and a dark version.
The map template ships this as a small helper:

```{r}
add_basemap <- function(map, mode = "light") {
  canvas <- function(layer) {
    sprintf(paste0("https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/",
                   "Canvas/World_%s_Gray_%s/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}"),
            if (mode == "dark") "Dark" else "Light", layer)
  }
  tiles <- tileOptions(maxNativeZoom = 16)   # the canvas stops at zoom 16
  map |>
    addTiles(canvas("Base"), options = tiles,
             attribution = "Tiles &copy; Esri &mdash; Esri, DeLorme, NAVTEQ") |>
    addTiles(canvas("Reference"), options = tiles)   # place names
}

output$map <- renderLeaflet({
  mode <- dm$mode()
  pal <- colorNumeric(brand_pal_seq("warm", n = 9, mode = mode), domain = d$value)

  leaflet(d) |>
    add_basemap(mode) |>
    addCircleMarkers(~lng, ~lat, color = ~pal(value), fillOpacity = 0.7) |>
    addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = ~value)
})
```

## Templates

There is one template per wrapper. Each writes a bslib-format `_brand.yml`, an
`app.R` and any local font and logo files into `path` (created if it doesn't
exist), then tells you how to run it. Nothing is overwritten unless you pass
`overwrite = TRUE`, and there is no stylesheet to copy: the wrappers load their
CSS at runtime.

```{r}
create_brand_shiny_app(path = "my-app")
shiny::runApp("my-app")
```

| Template | Wrapper | Shows | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `create_brand_shiny_app()` | `brand_page_sidebar(style = "drift")` | sidebar inputs, one scatter plot as a ggplot and as a `brand_plotly()` widget, a palette swatch, ornaments | `plotly` |
| `create_brand_shiny_dashboard()` | `brand_page_navbar()` | a row of value boxes, charts, three tabs, a DT table | `DT` |
| `create_brand_shiny_map()` | `brand_page_fluid()` | a leaflet colour ramp, tiles that follow the mode, `brand_plotly()` | `leaflet`, `plotly` |
| `create_brand_shiny_steps()` | `brand_page_sidebar(style = "drift")` | a workflow in order: numbered pills in the sidebar, Back / Next buttons | nothing extra |

The templates use R's built-in `airquality` data as their sample, except the map,
which needs coordinates and uses `quakes`. A template that needs a suggested package says so when you scaffold it instead of
failing at app start; the files are written either way.
